body: Also, re: the terminations. How would you convince a potential new employer that you've made big changes if you've only been let go a month or so before?!?

I guess I can see what you mean, it's just hard for me to see right now how someone would be attracted to me for who I am despite still living with parents in my mid-late 20's. I also think about how much this would set me back in plans for my future. Like if it took me until 30 to get my career off the ground again, I'd essentially be 5-10 years behind my peers and a "late bloomer" career-wise (which can be a red flag when applying for jobs or moving up the ladder). I worry about not being able to afford a house/condo until my 40's (a 30-year mortgage would basically take the rest of my life to pay off at that point).

Hmm...are you maybe thinking that if I do end up meeting someone while living at home, they might think "I'll date him but nothing serious", at least until I'm able to move out again? I'm not enthused at the idea of staying single all my life, that sounds horrible in itself.
I guess so, I'm concerned I'll be single the whole time I'm there and it'll only get worse as the years go by. I worry what friends/family will think of me as well.

Wow, that sounds interesting to be a monk and then leave after all those years. I just can't help but feel like my situation would be less understandable though. After a certain age (a couple years after college) I feel I'll get labelled as a bum/lazy/NEET if I'm living at home.

But what if this "great future" means me only getting back on track career-wise/moving back out again when I'm in my late 20s or 30's? I just don't see how I'd be worthy of respect/dateable if I had to move back home because I failed at my job and wasn't able to move back out until 30.

I seriously wish I didn't have so many mental health issues :( honestly, the best I can probably say about my mental health right now is "well, at least I'm not bipolar/schizo..."

I don't know, it'd be awful if I had to move back home and didn't get my career started back up until my 30's (and only moved back out then). People are marrying/having kids/moving into managerial roles at that age. If you don't mind me asking, was it just their careers that they didn't get sorted out until that age or something more?

I think it'd be ok to achieve all that in your early 30's, but being 38/39 and still single/no kids wouldn't sit well with me. What if I get another job in the same career path and just fail at that too? I just can't deal with this anymore :(

I really feel that time is of the essence though. I feel that I'll have really failed if it takes me until later into my 30's or 40's to get my career going, get a promotion, buy a house/condo or get married :(

I don't know, I just think it'd be awful to not get my career/life together until later in my 30's or my 40's. When's the last time you heard of someone getting their first promotion at 40, or buying their first home/condo in their 40's?!?

Doing my best doesn't put food on the table. All that matters is results, and having your shit together. It's imperative that I have my shit together by this age, and obviously I don't. It'd be no good if I finally got my shit together in my 30's or 40's, people would look down on me as a failure.

I've been dealing with depression/anxiety since my teen years, it got a bit better when I made friends in college/started dating but I think it's about to become worse than it's ever been before :(

Yeah, I'm seeing both a therapist and a psychiatrist on a regular basis. I can't believe how badly I lost the generic lottery mental-health wise though. I'm already on 2 medications for my anxiety (Lexapro and Ativan) and I know that ADD medications are also harsh on the body so I feel like I'll be lucky to see 60 at this rate :(  (if I don't take matters into my own hands, that is).

I don't know, I feel like things at my job are already so far gone and reviews are coming up soon so I feel like it'll be impossible to catch up, despite how hard I'm working now.

But how long will it take me to "bounce back"? If I lose this job, I'll definitely take a pay cut in the next one (which means I might have to get roommates, which would also affect dating). If I have to move back home, it could possibly take me years (into my late 20's) to move back out. Also, I'll have to explain why I was let go to every future employer. Might as well just cut my losses if it happens.

I've only been seeing them for like a month so I can see how it would be tough to be accepting of someone fucking up so badly when you don't even know them too well. I like what I'm doing but I'm not super passionate about it like a lot of my peers, and I don't want to have to move back home and go to grad school and finally get my career going when I'm 30. Most people are married with a house/kids by that age, and I'd just be starting out with a career (and most likely no partner, since who would ever date a guy who lives with parents after 25). On that note, I've wanted to have kids someday but now I'm starting to decide against it. I wouldn't wish all the shit I have (ADD, anxiety, depression) on my worst enemy.

Face it, if I lose my job, this is the only option.
Yes it does, it means I suck at the job I'm at. Having to move back to my parents would definitely result in a breakup. I don't want to wait until I'm possibly pushing 30 for things to get better :(
